content.title: What is Exception Handling?
content.description: Exception Handling is a mechanism in Java that allows programs to detect, handle, and recover from runtime errors without terminating unexpectedly.

content.content: During program execution, unexpected situations such as dividing by zero, accessing an invalid array index, or reading a missing file may occur. These situations are called exceptions. Java provides exception handling using try, catch, finally, throw, and throws to ensure programs remain stable and continue execution whenever possible.

content.title: Why Learn Exception Handling?
content.content: Proper exception handling improves application reliability, prevents crashes, simplifies debugging, and provides a better user experience.
What is an Exception?
An exception is an object that represents an abnormal condition during program execution. When an exception occurs, Java interrupts the normal flow and searches for a matching exception handler.

content.title: Exception Example
Key Idea
content.description: Exceptions are objects that describe runtime errors and can be handled to prevent program termination.

content.content: Types of Exceptions
Java classifies exceptions into checked exceptions, unchecked exceptions, and errors.
The try-catch Block
The try block contains code that may throw an exception. If an exception occurs, control transfers to the matching catch block.

content.title: try-catch Example

content.content: The finally Block
The finally block executes whether an exception occurs or not. It is commonly used for resource cleanup such as closing files or database connections.

content.title: finally Example
Best Practice
content.content: Use the finally block to release resources such as files, sockets, and database connections.
throw and throws
The throw keyword explicitly throws an exception, while throws declares that a method may pass an exception to its caller.

content.title: throws Example

content.content: Multiple Catch Blocks
A single try block can have multiple catch blocks to handle different types of exceptions.

content.content: Common Exceptions

items.question: ArithmeticException
items.answer: Occurs when an illegal arithmetic operation such as division by zero is performed.

items.question: NullPointerException
items.answer: Occurs when attempting to use a null reference.

items.question: ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException
items.answer: Occurs when accessing an invalid array index.

items.question: NumberFormatException
items.answer: Occurs when converting an invalid string into a number.

content.content: Checked vs Unchecked Exceptions
Real-Life Analogy

content.title: Car Safety Features
content.content: A seatbelt and airbag cannot prevent every accident, but they reduce damage and allow passengers to stay safe. Similarly, exception handling cannot stop errors from occurring, but it allows the program to recover gracefully.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Exception handling is a core Java interview topic. Questions commonly cover checked vs unchecked exceptions, try-catch-finally, throw vs throws, custom exceptions, and the exception hierarchy.
Common Mistakes

items.question: Can a try block exist without catch or finally?
items.answer: No. A try block must be followed by at least one catch block or a finally block.

items.question: Should Exception be caught everywhere?
items.answer: No. Catch specific exceptions whenever possible.

items.question: Does finally always execute?
items.answer: Yes, except in rare situations such as JVM termination.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: Use try for risky code, catch to handle exceptions, finally for cleanup, throw to create exceptions, and throws to declare possible exceptions.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: throws declares exceptions that a method may produce.
Checked exceptions are verified by the compiler, while unchecked exceptions occur at runtime.
